text:
Seth Jarvis has played only 13 of Carolina's games, and the ones he has played come with a theme. "Jarvis is creating so many chances and they're just not going for him right now," North State Journal's Cory Lavalette posted after Saturday's win over the Rangers, two nights after NHL.com's clip of Devon Levi robbing him.

The numbers agree. He has 2 goals on 24 shots, an 8.3% shooting rate against a likely range of 11 to 16%, and 10 points overall. At 5v5 the Hurricanes take 58% of the expected goals with him on the ice. That's a lot of territory, though Carolina is a puck-dominant team and he's a couple of points below his teammates there.

The thing to watch is ice time: he dropped to about 14 minutes in three of his last six games after playing 20 in others. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 42nd among forwards in wins above replacement, helped by strong linemates and by drawing more penalties than he takes, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries. The goals should follow the chances.
